## Natural history notes

A shrubby, strap-like lichen characterized by pale gray-green flattened branches that hang or project from bark, often with narrow lobes and small spore-producing structures along the branches. In Florida, it is found growing on tree bark and branches in humid forests, hammocks, swamps, mangroves, parks, and other wooded habitats with good air flow and moisture. Like other lichens, it is a symbiotic association between a fungus and photosynthetic partner, absorbing moisture and nutrients from the air while using trees mainly as a surface for attachment rather than as food.
